critical_code_review_comments: routes/dev_os.py still 1 244 lines after the split — over the 700-line soft cap. The split moved 30 routes out; consider further extracting projects/env-vars/talk/templates into per-domain routers so each file stays under ~600 lines.

routes/dev_gates.py POST /gates/run response shape is {qa, security, ok, ran_at, smoke?} — NOT a top-level list/object of 'gates' or 'checks'. Frontend and integrators may expect a canonical 'checks: [...]' array; consider adding one for API-shape consistency with /smoke-test (which returns {checks: [...]}).

Several moved endpoints return envelope objects while their siblings return bare arrays: GET /dev-projects/{id}/files → {count, files:[...]}, GET /release-notes → {releases:[...]}, GET /files/{id}/snapshots → {snapshots:[...]}, GET /audit-log → {entries:[...]}. But GET /dev-tasks and GET /improvement-proposals return bare lists. Pick ONE convention repo-wide; frontend already handles both but the inconsistency is a foot-gun for new callers.

dev_os_preview.py serve_preview at line 154 uses {file_path:path} — good — but there is no explicit content-security-policy header on the served HTML/JS. Since these are user-generated apps served under the parent origin, a stray <script src='https://evil'> in a generated file executes in the same origin as the auth cookie. Consider serving preview/share content with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox or via a distinct subdomain.

dev_publish.py GET /p-resolve is unauthenticated and flips domain_status → connected on the FIRST hit for any host that matches an unconfirmed domain. That means an attacker who guesses a customer's pending domain can auto-confirm it without any DNS proof. Recommend an actual TXT/CNAME probe before flipping status = 'connected'.

dev_os_tasks.py line 169 role-claims handler now defaults role_claims to {} when the project field is missing (verified fix). Good. Suggest also normalising to an empty dict in the write-side patch_production/publish paths so downstream code never has to null-check.

rca of the issue: No blocking bugs identified in this iteration. After fixing the assertions the full suite is green. The only environmental caveat is the same EMERGENT_LLM_KEY $20 budget cap called out in iteration_76 — my talk-endpoint test guards on 402 / 'budget' and skips gracefully. Router split was clean: no dropped routes, no auth-scope changes, no data-shape regressions. Custom-domain flow works end-to-end (publish→PATCH→p-resolve→connected). Template live demo works for ap-ledger and correctly 404s for saas-dashboard (which has no code template).
